data.description:
## Summary

Two defects in one place, found while mitigating the tickets-branch write storm.

**1. The documented rollback names a table that is never parsed.** `rebar.toml:38` tells operators
to scope the enrichment drain with:

    [tool.rebar.llm] overlap_drain = "off"

That table does not exist in this config's schema. The real table is `[llm]` (`rebar.toml:198`).
An operator who follows the instruction gets **no error and no effect** — the key is silently
ignored and the drain keeps running at its `async` default. Verified by resolving the effective
config against both table names on the same file:

    [tool.rebar.llm] overlap_drain = "always"  ->  effective 'async'   (NOT parsed)
    [llm]            overlap_drain = "always"  ->  effective 'always'  (parsed)

The failure is silent in a second way: `_llm_drain_mode` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:447`) maps any
unrecognized value back to the default, so a typo also reads as "enrichment is off" while it is on.

**2. The shipped default floods the shared branch.** With `suggest_duplicate_tickets = true`
(`rebar.toml:39`) and `overlap_drain` unset, every ticket write path spawns an opportunistic drain
(`src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:505` `maybe_drain`). Each enrichment cycle appends and separately
pushes `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` -> `CLAIM_ENRICH` -> `TICKET_DIGEST` -> `DONE_ENRICH`, so ~4 pushed commits
per ticket. Measured on `origin/tickets`: ~1000-1400 commits/hour sustained since 2026-08-27
21:00 UTC, against a prior baseline of ~20-90/hour.

That write rate starves every other writer. A fetch->merge->push recovery cycle costs 2.4-4.2s
while competing pushes land every 2-4s, so a writer that falls behind never regains the lead. The
observed consequence was stores diverging without bound (one clone reached 619 unpushed commits)
and cross-environment reads disagreeing — a signed ticket read as `unsigned` through the MCP
server while the local store showed a valid `completion-verifier` attestation.

## Scope

Set `overlap_drain = "off"` in the committed `[llm]` table, and correct the comment that names the
wrong table. This is the project's own documented scoping knob, not a new mechanism:
`suggest_duplicate_tickets` stays `true`, so plan-review keeps its advisory overlap suggestions;
only the opportunistic drain on ordinary write paths stops. `maybe_drain` returns at
`enrich_drain.py:525` before spawning anything.

Explicitly OUT of scope: the retry/backoff defects and the store's failure to converge
(`cibophobic-moist-guineafowl`, `b928-3ab6-5985-417b`). This ticket reduces the write pressure
that exposed them; it does not fix them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar.toml`'s `[llm]` table sets `overlap_drain = "off"`, and resolving the effective
      config against the repo root returns `'off'` (checked by running the config resolver, not
      by grepping the file — an invalid value silently falls back to the default).
- [ ] The comment at `rebar.toml:38` names `[llm]`, the table that is actually parsed, so an
      operator following it gets the effect it describes.
- [ ] A regression test pins that `overlap_drain` is read from the `[llm]` table and that an
      unparsed table name does NOT silently yield the default — the specific trap here is that
      "wrong table" and "correct table set to the default" are indistinguishable from the
      resolved value alone, so the test must use a non-default value to discriminate.
- [ ] `suggest_duplicate_tickets` remains `true` and plan-review's advisory overlap path is
      unchanged (checked: the existing overlap tests still pass).

## Evidence

Effective config on the three deployed writer containers was `async` before the change and `off`
after, read via the resolver inside each container rather than from file text.
data.title: rebar.toml documents a never-parsed table for overlap_drain, and the drain default floods the shared tickets branch
